the scenario's own notes specify a SECOND, hand-constructed adversarial RewriteRule (not in producers.js -- an ad-hoc addition per the scenario's stated purpose, 'this engine's mandatory adversarial case'): lhs matches any nonnil_binding(self,_) term regardless of second arg, rhs canonicalizes/merges it into ONE shared class nonnil_binding_by_name(self), discarding which defining function it came from

the order in which this second rule fires relative to any per-site supports-polarity attachment is NOT specified anywhere in the design doc -- §4's non-confluence discussion names order-dependence as an open, unresolved property of Reading B generally, not something this document pins down; I picked: (a) honest rewrite for A, (b) honest rewrite for B, (c) both individually acquire a supports polarity from their own rule firing (A's rule still can't see the counterexample; B's rule is genuinely sound here), (d) THEN the adversarial merge rule collapses both classes into nonnil_binding_by_name(self)

steps.description: post-merge: nonnil_binding_by_name(self) is now the SAME store entry for what were A's and B's terms -- this is the destructive, irreversible egraph-style merge the design doc names explicitly; the term store's identity structure no longer distinguishes 'self at Cache:peek' from 'self at Deque:pop_front'

conflict check on the merged class: both original terms independently carried supports (no refutes anywhere in this rule set, per producers.js), so the merged class carries only supports -- not a conflict in the ⊥ sense, but a silent identification: B's genuinely-supported polarity now reads back as if it also independently corroborates A, and A's real counterexample (which was never even representable as a refuting term) is doubly invisible now that A and B's site identities are gone from the store

verdict: the merged canonical representative is Proved.
